description: Free. Ranks the library’s parts for a job described in words, with why each fits and what it costs on the target platform (median ms a frame at 1920×1080 on a measured machine and tier). Strong matches for the job come first (each part says match: strong or loose, and which of the job’s words it matched), then looser ones; when nothing plainly does the job, every result is loose and nothingFits says so: build that piece yourself rather than force a part to fit; within each, parts that fit the platform and budget lead, then those over the budget (overBudget), then those that need WebGPU on a platform without it (blocked). For an interface job, 3D, simulation and effects parts rank lower. Each part says what it runs in (runsIn): raw WebGPU passes, a three.js scene, a 2D canvas or the DOM; a three.js part needs a three.js app, so check it against your renderer before installing. When the words name a look or ask for one, the matching looks come back too. Search by the job, not by a name.

approach.description: Optional: follow (the default: the library as it is) or inspire (your own concept first; parts and looks as references; default rules as advice). Accessibility and the licence bind in both. Also settable once as /mcp?approach=inspire.

budget.description: Ms a frame the part may cost on that platform (the worse of GPU and CPU).

job.description: What the part has to do, e.g. "date range filter for a dashboard" or "grass that bends round a walker".

kit.description: Optional: a kit id (e.g. dashboard) to search only its parts and those of the kits it is built on.

platform.description: The target: desktop (the reference laptop, the default), laptop (integrated GPU), phone, a machine id from a part’s costs, or "no-webgpu" for browsers without it.

name: find_parts
title: Find parts for a job
